newsitem.title: UK: Soggy mark, U.S. trade data buoy dlr at Euro close.
newsitem.headline: Soggy mark, U.S. trade data buoy dlr at Euro close.

text.p: The dollar soared to near 31-month highs versus the mark on Friday, buoyed by better-than-expected U.S. trade data, analysts said.

The backbone of the dollar rise has been the mark's slide on its European crosses but the spark to fuel its rally above 1.61 marks came from November trade data. The trade deficit rose 4.9 percent to $8.4 billion, below the $9.8 billion gap forecast.
"The weak mark has been the driving force behind the dollar's rally, and the trade data gave it even more impetus," said Chris Furness, foreign exchange strategist at 4Cast.

The dollar soared to its highest level since June 1994 at 1.6125 marks after slicing through tough resistance at 1.6060, a 61.8 percent Fibonacci retracement of its decline from 1.7686 in February 1994 to the record low at 1.3430 in March 1995.
It had already recovered most of its losses from late Thursday, helped by a mark drop to fresh lows in its current downmove versus the Norway crown, sterling and the lira.

The trade data spurred some economists to upgrade their estimates for fourth-quarter U.S. economic growth. December industrial production data, showing a rise of 0.8 percent against 0.6 percent expected, underlined the bullish scenario.
At 1615 GMT the dollar traded at 1.6120/25 marks and 117.25/30 yen, compared with 1.5952/62 and 116.49/54 in late European trading on Thursday.
Dollar/yen also benefited from the data but was capped by talk of offers around 117.40/50 yen. The politically sensitive deficit with Japan dropped 12.9 percent to $4.32 billion.

Concern that the Bank of Japan might be on the offer soon continued to haunt dollar/yen, dealers said. Reported comments by a Japanese ministry of finance official, saying Japan was unwilling to sell dollars in the open market, did little to dispel those fears.
"There is some talk in the market about the BOJ but in the short-term dollar/yen has scope to move higher as well," said Robert Prior, economist at HSBC James Capel in London.
General dollar enthusiasm is expected to carry the dollar to 120 yen but the slide of mark/yen has been a dampener.
The mark was down one percent against the yen from Wednesday's highs after a recovery attempt ran out of steam. It last traded at 72.67/69, down from 73.00/03 late on Thursday.
The focus for next week will be on economic data out of Germany and Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony before the U.S. Senate on Tuesday.
Greenspan's testimony will be the week's pivotal point for markets after a batch of strong economic numbers heightened speculation of a rise in U.S. interest rates, analysts said.
Further clues about the direction of German interest rates are expected from German M3 money supply data for December due for release next week.

The fortnightly Bundesbank council meeting on Thursday will be closely eyed as usual but even more so after remarks this week by council member Hans-Juergen Krupp, dealers said. Krupp said Germany's high unemployment showed in what a grave state the economy was, which could not be ignored by the Bundesbank.
The Ifo German business sentiment survey for December, another key indicator, is expected on Tuesday.
More signs of weakness in the German economy coupled with evidence of low-inflationary growth in the U.S. will help to underscore the dollar's bullish tone, analysts said.
Kleinwort Benson economist Reiner Back updated his dollar forecast this week, based on firm U.S. economic data, mounting EMU optimism and a restrictive Japanese budget.
Back said in a note to clients the dollar was now poised to enter a range between 1.64 and 1.67 marks. For dollar/yen, he sees scope to 120 yen, where strong yen support cuts in.
